page: Microsoft Azure D2pds_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DPDSv5 family, powered by an ARM64 architecture. It features 2 dedicated physical cores on an Ampere Neoverse-N1 processor running at 3.0 GHz, with 1.0 thread per core. The hardware configuration includes 8.0 GB of RAM, which equates to 4.0 GB per core, alongside 77 GB of local storage and support for Premium Storage. The CPU contains 64 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark results indicate modest performance characteristics. Single-core performance is average, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1822.18 and single-threaded gzip compression at 24.14 GB/sec. However, multi-core and memory-intensive operations show limitations. The stress-ng multi-core score is 3612.77, and the Geekbench multi-core score is 2008.0, both falling into the lower performance tiers. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with read-only large block bandwidth at 24.09 GB/sec and write large block bandwidth at 15.78 GB/sec.

Given its dedicated ARM-based cores and low-tier multi-threaded performance, this server offers a cost-efficient entry point for workloads that do not require x86 compatibility or high-intensity parallel processing. It is suitable for lightweight, single-threaded tasks, basic static web serving, and simple database operations. It is less suited for memory-bound applications, complex multi-threaded computations, or LLM inference, where it exhibits poor performance metrics.
